arxiv-2103-13016.title: Stability, convergence and bifurcation in some models of chemical kinetics
arxiv-2103-13016.creator: Abuthahir Abdulrahuman, Kalyan Sundar Chakrabarti, Gaurav Raina
arxiv-2103-13016.description: Abstract In this paper, we analyze the stability, convergence, and bifurcation properties of the Boissonade-De Kepper (BD) model which played a key role in the development of nonlinear chemical dynamics. We first outline conditions for local stability, which may help guide design considerations. Then, we show that the BD model undergoes a Hopf bifurcation when the stability condition gets violated.

arxiv-2111-14539.title: STUDY OF SMALL PERTURBATIONS OF A STATIONARY STATE IN A MODEL OF UPPER HYBRID PLASMA OSCILLATIONS
arxiv-2111-14539.creator: Olga S. Rozanova
arxiv-2111-14539.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Olga S. Rozanova. It is shown that a constant external magnetic field, generally speaking, is not able to prevent breaking (loss of smoothness) of relativistic plasma oscillations, even if they are arbitrarily small perturbations of the zero steady state. This result sharply differs from the non-relativistic case, for which it is possible to suppress the breaking of oscillations at any initial deviations by increasing the intensity of the magnetic field [ 13 ] .

arxiv-2204-06999.title: “Double-path” ferroelectrics and the sign of the piezoelectric response
arxiv-2204-06999.creator: Yubo Qi 1 , Sebastian E. Reyes-Lillo 2 , and Karin M. Rabe 1
arxiv-2204-06999.description: Abstract In this work, we propose a class of ferroelectrics (which we denote “double-path” ferroelectrics), characterized by two competing polarization switching paths for which the change in polarization is different and in fact of opposite sign. Depending on which path is favorable under given conditions, this leads to different identification of up- and down-polarized states.

arxiv-2208-02551.title: HÖLDER AND LIPSCHITZ CONTINUITY IN ORLICZ-SOBOLEV CLASSES, DISTORTION AND HARMONIC MAPPINGS
arxiv-2208-02551.creator: MIODRAG MATELJEVIC, RUSLAN SALIMOV
arxiv-2208-02551.description: Abstract In this article, we consider the Hölder continuity of injective maps in Orlicz-Sobolev classes defined on the unit ball. Under certain conditions on the growth of dilatations, we obtain the Hölder continuity of the indicated class of mappings. In particular, under certain special restrictions, we show that Lipschitz continuity of mappings holds.

arxiv-2305-12415.description: Abstract . We describe a construction of three-dimensional Hadamard matrices of even order v v such that v − 1 v-1 is a prime power. The construction covers infinitely many orders for which the existence was previously open. 1991 Mathematics Subject Classification 05B20, 15B34 1.

For EIT, one of the most important research directions is degree of freedom (DoF) analysis.

pmc-11351131.title: Pathways from Family Functioning to Internet Gaming Disorder: The Mediating Role of the Dark Triad
pmc-11351131.creator: Danilo Calaresi, Valeria Verrastro, Fiorenza Giordano, Janine Gullo, Valeria Saladino, Xiaochun Xie
pmc-11351131.description: With internet gaming disorder (IGD) becoming more common, there are growing worries about the health of those it affects. This study examines how traits like Machiavellianism, psychopathy, and narcissism might connect family functioning to IGD. The research involved 1190 young adults who answered an online survey, sharing their personal experiences.

pmc-11386467.title: “I probably shouldn’t go in today”: Inequitable access to paid sick leave and its impacts on health behaviors during the emergence of COVID-19 in the Seattle area
pmc-11386467.creator: Chidozie D. Iwu, Sarah N. Cox, Sarah L. Sohlberg, Ashley E. Kim, Jennifer Logue, Peter D. Han, Thomas R. Sibley, Misja Ilcisin, Kairsten A. Fay, Jover Lee, Denise J. McCulloch, Yongzhe Wang, Michael Boeckh, Janet A. Englund, Lea M. Starita, Anjum Hajat, Helen Y. Chu
pmc-11386467.description: This study examines inequities in access to paid sick leave (PSL) by race/ethnicity, income, and sex and the role of PSL access on leave-taking and care-seeking behaviors among Seattle-area workers in the months leading up to and during the emergence of COVID-19 in the region.

pmc-11417415.title: Diagnostic Modalities in Heart Failure: A Narrative Review
pmc-11417415.creator: Tanisha, Chaithanya Amudha, Mohammed Raake, Dany Samuel, Sulakshna Aggarwal, Zainab M Din Bashir, Karabo K Marole, Iqra Maryam, Zahra Nazir
pmc-11417415.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Heart failure (HF) can present acutely or progress over time. It can lead to morbidity and mortality affecting 6.5 million Americans over the age of 20. The HF type is described according to the ejection fraction classification, defined as the percentage of blood volume that exits the left ventricle after myocardial contraction, undergoing ejection into the circulation, also called stroke volume, and is proportional to the ejection fraction. Cardiac catheterization is an invasive procedure to evaluate coronary artery disease leading to HF.

pmc-12598186.title: Primary Dural Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma: A Case Report
pmc-12598186.creator: Yoshiaki Takamura, Takatoshi Fujimoto
pmc-12598186.description: Primary dural lymphoma is a rare subtype of primary central nervous system lymphoma that arises from the dura mater. The majority of primary dural lymphomas are histologically mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue lymphoma. We present a rare case of a 78-year-old woman with primary dural lymphoma diagnosed as diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. She was admitted with status epilepticus.

pmc-12692404.title: Computational Phenotypic Drug Discovery for Anticancer Chemotherapy: PTML Modeling of Multi-Cell Inhibitors of Colorectal Cancer Cell Lines
pmc-12692404.creator: Alejandro Speck-Planche, M Natália D S Cordeiro, Antonio Rescifina
pmc-12692404.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Colorectal cancer is one of the most dangerous neoplastic diseases in terms of both mortality and incidence. Thus, anti-colorectal cancer agents are urgently needed. Computational approaches have great potential to accelerate the phenotypic discovery of versatile anticancer agents. Here, by combining perturbation-theory machine learning (PTML) modeling with the fragment-based topological design (FBTD) approach, we provide key computational evidence on the computer-aided de novo design and prediction of new molecules virtually exhibiting multi-cell inhibitory activity against different colorectal cancer cell lines.

pmc-12756757.title: Preparation and Performance Evaluation of Intelligent Oil Displacement Janus Nanosheets
pmc-12756757.creator: Shoufei Lu, Meilong Fu, Yanmin Mi, Changhai Cui
pmc-12756757.description: To enhance the recovery factor in low-permeability reservoirs and address the challenge of nanoparticle adsorption at interfaces, a smart oil displacement Janus nanosheet was synthesized using a template method. The Janus nanosheets possess an amphiphilic structure, with one side being hydrophilic due to carboxyl groups and the other side being hydrophobic due to alkyl groups.

pmc-12764921.title: Cancer stage at diagnosis by duration of pre-existing chronic analgesic use and anxiety or depression
pmc-12764921.creator: Helen Fowler, Georgios Lyratzopoulos, Meena Rafiq, Matthew E. Barclay, Gary A. Abel, Cristina Renzi
pmc-12764921.description: Pre-existing chronic diseases may delay or expedite cancer diagnosis. Here, we examine variations in cancer stage at diagnosis based on duration and type of common chronic conditions. We identify lung and colon cancers diagnosed 2012-2018 from national cancer registration, and pre-existing physical and mental-health conditions from linked primary care records.

pmc-12869853.title: High-Intensity Interval Training Enhances Cardiovascular and Functional Outcomes Compared With Moderate-Intensity Continuous Training in Higher-Functioning Chronic Stroke
pmc-12869853.creator: Hyun-min Moon
pmc-12869853.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ObjectiveTo compare the effects of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) and moderate-intensity continuous training (MICT) on cardiovascular function, gait ability, and hematological variables in chronic stroke survivors.MethodsTwenty-nine higher-functioning, ambulatory chronic stroke survivors were randomized to HIIT (n=15) or MICT (n=14). Participants underwent supervised training three times weekly for six weeks, consisting of 30 minutes conventional therapy followed by 40 minutes aerobic exercise (HIIT: six 1-minute high-intensity intervals at 80%–100% maximum heart rate (HRmax) with 4-minute active recovery; MICT: continuous exercise at 60%–80% HRmax).

pmc-13290340.title: Comparative prognostic performance of quick sequential organ failure assessment, lactate, systemic inflammatory response syndrome criteria, and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio for mortality prediction in critically ill dogs and cats
pmc-13290340.creator: Burin Boonsri, Thanatcha Chaengcheroen, Jidapa Jitprasert, Charisa Suriyawong, Pinkarn Chantawong
pmc-13290340.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background and Aim:Early identification of critically ill dogs and cats at high-risk of mortality is essential for timely intervention and improved clinical outcomes in veterinary emergency and critical-care practice. Several prognostic indicators, including the quick sequential organ failure assessment (qSOFA), blood lactate concentration, systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS) criteria, and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), have been proposed for risk-stratification; however, comparative evidence in mixed populations of critically ill small animals remains limited.

pmc-13316679.title: Sprayable lipid-based lubricated hydrogel coating for alleviating catheter-related mucosal damage and pain
pmc-13316679.creator: Sufang Chen, Haixia Wang, Jingyi Du, Jinyan Guo, Jing Yang, Ni Ding, Zhenjia Lin, Yuzhuo Hei, Yu Tao, Ziqing Hei, Gangjian Luo, Mingqiang Li, Weifeng Yao
pmc-13316679.description: Medical catheters are essential for clinical diagnosis and therapy, yet their insertion and retention inevitably cause mucosal damage and pain. Conventional catheters compromise comfort and risk secondary inflammation, underscoring the need for advanced catheter surface coatings. Herein, we developed a sprayable lipid-based lubricated hydrogel coating (Oxy@Lipo/Gel) by integrating oxybuprocaine-loaded liposomes (Oxy@Lipo) with an oxidized hyaluronic acid/carboxymethyl chitosan (OHA/CMCS) hydrogel.
